stops.title: A reference paper
stops.text: This tab is a reference paper, so it is background reading, not one of your assigned articles. Qwen3-Omni is what a full omni model looks like: one model that reads text, images, audio and video, and can answer in streaming speech. Before we open it, let me give you four ideas the authors take for granted.

stops.title: Big model, small compute
stops.text: The first idea is mixture of experts. The name thirty B A three B means thirty billion parameters in total, but a router sends each token to only a few experts, so about three billion do the work. Notice the catch in the bottom bar: every expert still has to sit in memory. At four bits that is about fifteen gigabytes, so this one will not fine-tune on a free T4.

stops.title: How a model speaks
stops.text: The second idea is speaking in codec tokens. For every eighty milliseconds of speech, the Talker predicts one code, a small module fills in fifteen more, and a decoder called Code2Wav turns them into sound straight away. That is why the paper can report a first sound after about two hundred thirty four milliseconds. Your own task only needs text answers, so you can ignore this half.

stops.title: Words to know
stops.text: Keep the glossary close. Thinker is the language model that understands, and Talker is the part that speaks. AuT is the new audio encoder that replaces Whisper, and TM-RoPE gives every token a position on a real time axis. And watch for word error rate, W E R, because your normalization experiment will show how much it depends on cleaning the text.

stops.title: Where this paper sits
stops.text: Finally, where are we in the atlas? This is paper nine of eleven. It builds straight on Qwen2.5-Omni from the last tab, keeps the Thinker and Talker split, and upgrades almost every part. It takes all three of your inputs natively, plus video. Next comes MiniCPM-o 4.5. When you're ready, press Play guided tour.
